Risk of Rain is a very special game, guaranteed to throw your emotions in a swing like back in kindergarten during recess. To cite from their website riskofraingame.com, "Risk of Rain is an action/platformer with randomized elements." The randomized elemets are everything from the level design to the enemies you fight as well as the items that power up your character. The goal of the game is to survive all 5 randomized levels and beat each boss in their level respectively, all within one life. This is where the game becomes both challenging and addictive. Once your character drops below zero HP, you die and lose all of your progress in that playthrough. But with every end, there is a new beginning. When you first start out, you are limited to one character, the Commando. The more you play the game, the more items you can unlock which, given your character's set skills, can either compliment your playthrough or feel like an unecessary add on. One could also unlock more characters, like the Enforcer or Bandit, who have different playstyles. As with all games, the more time you sink into it, the better you can be, which also brings up another very important aspect of the game, 'time'. When you start your playthrough say for example on Easy, there is a bar on the rightside of the screen with a time gauge. It starts out at the bottom saying Very Easy. This difficulty meter is separate from the initial choice made from the start of the game. The longer you play in the game, the more the meter grows. What does the meter do? It dictates how frequent the monsters spawn and how strong they could be. Starting out it's nothing to be concerned with, as most enemy mobs are weak and managable. However, as time passes, more monsters spawn and different varieties of the same monster spawn, giving more of a challenge to the player. This is in place to prevent players from staying in one level, 'grinding' to get gear and an advantage over the game. This game is by no stretch of the imagination easy. It is a very challenging game and the rewards for beating the game may not seem so plesant at first, but challenging yourself and enduring through the levels can grant you a sense of acomplishment that you may not get too much in real life.

Risk of Rain is well worth the purchase. It's brutal in the absolute best possible way, it doesn't cut you any slack but never feels unfair or cheap. When you die (which you will) it always feels like its your fault and there's something you could have done better to survive that little bit longer. Its immensely re-playable due to the random nature of the levels, although this is mostly through item type and placement rather than the actual layout itself. The pacing of the game is excellent, the early stages build up your confidence as you cut down the occasional enemy but as time goes on your plight becomes more and more desperate, until you're engaged in a frantic dash for survival during the boss fights.

Rounds are between 20-30 minutes in length, which makes it perfect for dipping into when you don't feel like sinking your teeth into something heavier. Adjusting the difficultly actually changes the whole feel of the game, going easier results in a very satisfying "god mode" with a huge array of items turning you into a powerhouse, whilst going harder is a constant adrenalin rush. I confess I'm not actully good enough to make any real progess on the hardest difficulty but its fun in a mascohistic way regardless. Credit must also go to the soundtrack, which is phenomenal and deeply atmospheric. The pixel art style is different and certainly striking, though might not be to everyone's taste but doesn't diminish the game at all.

My only minor compliant is that the ballance in the items can seem a bit off. Some are incredibly situational, bordering on useless whilst others are fantasic and near certain choices. Although the random nature of the game can result in you getting screwed over from time to time, it doesn't happen very often.

In short, a fantastic game which I'll probably still play years down the line, highly recommended.

The longer you stay on this hellhole of a planet, the tougher things will get.

But you're stranded. So. Please start moving.

The inherit challenge of Risk of Rain is to balance speed with thoroughness. Dwell any particular region longer and you're bound to discover (and be able to afford) an array of random weaponry which stacks together in clever ways, turning your hopeless vagrant into a prayed-for messiah. But there's that catch ... the longer you dwell in one zone, the more infernal the next will be. So as you fight simply to survive, you'll also be gauging time and charting hypothetical routes through the mysterious wasteland ... hoping to come across the right combination of moneys, chests and sacrificial totems in efficient order.

Aside from the planet's devious armory, your years on the frontier have supplied you with a certain set of skills. Regardless of your profession, these core skills usually take form in a weak-ish basic attack, a middling form of crowd control, some type of evasion, and a signature ability (think of this as the one that won you all that money on The Universe's Got Talent: Killing Edition). Each time you use a skill - beyond the basic attack - you'll have to wait a few seconds before you can use it again. As that one random monster crab is quickly joined by every casual acquiantance from his apparently quite-social life, those seconds can seem like an eternity. But you'll need to use those skills with abandon - conservation is for another time and place.

Again. Don't stop.

As your deaths accumulate, Risk of Rain becomes a game about learning the ins-and-outs of an alien frontier while constantly pushing yourself to discover new corners of its relentless universe. 

Your only choice of profession at the start is a fine-tuned but vanilla-bean commando. But just as you begin to master your skills, you'll unlock a new, entirely unique character to possibly nudge your game progress further. Trust those who have come before: The new characters will often feel useless on the first playthrough. At some point, you'll wrap your brain around the death-delivering potential of each. And as you pour gallons of acid across shadowy plains or single-shot the entire health bar of one of the game's gargantuan bosses, you will learn to feel invincible ... for a minute or two at least.

Each of the planet's progressively elaborate environments includes a familiar basic layout from play to play, but its random generation makes each play just uncomfortable enough to force you to make decisions on the fly. Level talk is boring, but do note: the surprisingly elaborate final stage is reward in itself.

Risk of Rain is a game that requires skill and cunning ... but not so much skill and cunning to be abusive. It drops a torrent of challenges on you ... while giving you delightful ways to overcome them. To this survivor: It's earned a place in the Roguelike Temple of Elders.

Be sure to visit.

Just remember to keep moving.
Had fun with games like FTL and/or Binding of Isaac? Then this is a game for you. Just buy it if you are even considering, and you will not regret it.
